title: IADR: Interface-Augmented Neural Operator for Phase-Field Mean-Curvature Flow
claim: A conditioning parameter is mapped by a hypernetwork to the weights of a structured target operator that advances the state each step.
layout: 3 nested panels, left-to-right, hypernetwork on top with diffusion-reaction flow below
description: A large dashed rounded box is split into three columns titled Inputs, IADR and Outputs. On the left, the Inputs column holds a stack of phase-field snapshots (a red star-shaped region on dark blue) labelled initial states q_t. Beneath it is a red-to-blue gradient square labelled ε, the interface width. The center IADR panel is orange. At the top is a neural network drawn as nodes. A single ε node feeds two hidden layers of orange nodes, which feed green output nodes. These lead to a purple Weights box showing w_D and w_R. A bracketed arrow carries the weights down to the bottom row. In that row, q_t flows through a Diffusion block D_{w_D}, then a Reaction block R_{w_R}, labelled the DR splitting operator. The right Outputs column shows stacked predicted frames q_{t+δt} and K-step rollout snapshots, with the shape smoothed to a rounded pentagon and then a circle. Arrows join the three columns.
caption: Overview of IADR: the hypernetwork $h_\vartheta(\varepsilon)$ emits the weights of the DR splitting network $\Phi = \mathcal{R}_{w_R} \circ \mathcal{D}_{w_D}$ (target network), which advances the phase field $q_\varepsilon(\cdot, t)$ by one time step and can be applied autoregressively for $K$-step rollout.
abstract: The Allen-Cahn equation is one of the standard phase-field models for mean-curvature flow (MCF), parameterised by the diffuse-interface width $\varepsilon$. Practical simulations span a range of $\varepsilon$, so a single model covering this range is needed. PDE-specific neural operators are accurate but must be retrained at every $\varepsilon$; general neural operators cover $\varepsilon$ in one model but lose the phase-field structure of the target. We introduce Interface-Augmented Diffusion-Reaction (IADR), a neural operator that addresses both shortcomings: a target network with a diffusion-and-reaction (DR) structure preserves the phase-field structure of the Allen-Cahn equation, while a hypernetwork that maps $\varepsilon$ to the weights of this target network amortises the dependence on $\varepsilon$ across the range. A single IADR matches the per-$\varepsilon$ specialists on in-distribution data within the prescribed range, retains their cross-shape generalisation under both $\varepsilon$- and geometry-out-of-distribution shifts, and retains their compact DR target structure with millisecond-scale inference. We further establish a conditional $K$-step rollout error bound under consistency and stability assumptions.
